fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Access Drive; Open Green Space; Garden Area; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Perimeter Fencing
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly on both sides so responders arriving under low-visibility conditions can locate it without delay.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the access drive so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Keep a turnaround area clear at or near the main residence so fire apparatus and emergency vehicles can exit without reversing the full length of the drive.
• Cut back vegetation that is growing close to the main residence and detached structure to reduce the chance of fire spreading directly to the buildings.
• Thin dense vegetation between the detached structure and the main residence so responders can move between buildings on foot.
• Clear a ground-level path along at least one side of the main residence so responders can reach the rear of the property on foot.
• Keep perimeter fence gates unlocked or fitted with a standard knox-box or breakaway latch so responders are not delayed at the fence line.
• Mark any fence gate that provides rear or side access with a reflective sign so responders can locate it quickly.
• Identify and maintain a clear area near the access drive where a second emergency vehicle can stage without blocking the primary route.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Brush Area; Mixed Vegetation; Open Green Space; Vegetation Near Structure; Grass Cover; Vegetation Along Driveway; Large Trees; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim shrubs scattered around the structure that are growing directly against or within a few feet of exterior walls.
• Cut back brush in the brush area where it connects with vegetation growing toward the structure.
• Remove dry or dead grass near the base of the structure and along the edges of paved or gravel surfaces.
• Trim overhanging branches from large trees that extend over the roofline or gutters.
• Keep the driveway clear of overhanging branches from trees and shrubs along both sides to allow emergency vehicle access.
• Mow or cut grass cover in open areas between vegetation and the structure to keep it short, especially during dry periods.
• Separate shrubs and small plants growing in mixed vegetation areas near the structure so there are visible gaps between individual plants.
• Remove any dead branches from large trees near the structure before they fall onto the roof or block access routes.
• Keep the single access route free of vegetation encroachment on both sides to maintain clear passage for vehicles.
• Thin vegetation along the driveway edges where shrubs or brush have grown close enough to brush against passing vehicles.
